condition: Acute coronary syndrome in pregnancy (spontaneous coronary artery dissection)
summary: 36-year-old woman at 33 weeks with sudden central chest pain radiating to the left arm and sweating while climbing stairs. SCAD is the commonest cause of pregnancy-associated MI.

inputs.hpi: 33 weeks pregnant (second pregnancy). One hour ago, climbing the stairs to clinic, sudden central chest tightness radiating to the left arm, with sweating and breathlessness. Still present, 7/10. Referred to surgical clinic for symptomatic gallstones earlier in pregnancy. No leg swelling. No headache or visual symptoms.

exam.cardiovascular: Pulse 108 regular, BP 128/82, heart sounds normal.
exam.abdomen: Gravid uterus consistent with dates, soft, non-tender.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected acute coronary syndrome in pregnancy (possible SCAD)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Sudden chest pain with arm radiation at 33 weeks - pregnancy-associated ACS (SCAD) to exclude; PE and aortic dissection also in differential.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: not in top 3 of web.pane: 1. Acute Cholecystitis | 2. Traumatic Pneumothorax | 3. GORD / Reflux Oesophagitis; also in web.symptomInference#2, web.passive#2. PANE (lib/pane-engine, 131 diseases) has no acute coronary syndrome node.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: lib/pane-engine: add an acute coronary syndrome node (chest pain / pressure, radiation to arm or jaw, diaphoresis, dyspnoea; age, diabetes and smoking modifiers) or a must-not-miss cross-check, and map I20-I24 in getProtocolByIcd.

mustNotMiss.note: Pregnancy chest pain: PE and aortic dissection are the other must-not-miss causes.
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: not in top 3 of web.pane: 1. Acute Cholecystitis | 2. Traumatic Pneumothorax | 3. GORD / Reflux Oesophagitis. PANE has PE but no aortic dissection node.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: PANE: add aortic dissection; let chest-pain SOCRATES answers reach pleuritic/chest features.

mustAlarm.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: no alarm names a cardiac cause. The only cardiac signals are the triage reason "Possible cardiac event" and the Chest Pain Pathway panel title; every safety prompt raised is non-cardiac (Emergency now, Pre-operative assessment, and e.g. "Hernia - elective repair indicated", "Reproductive-age female with abdominal complaint", "Creatinine elevated").
mustAlarm.proposedFix: rules.ts / clinical-inference.ts: an ACS rule that fires on chest pain/pressure OR (dyspnoea, jaw/arm pain, epigastric pain, sweating or unexplained fatigue in a patient >=50, diabetic or female) -> emergency_now with "12-lead ECG within 10 minutes + hs-troponin; 999/ED transfer".

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: no ECG investigation. The triage Chest Pain Pathway panel does fire here and its checklist text reads "ECG within 10 minutes", "Troponin (hs-cTnI/T) at 0h and 3h" and "Aspirin 300mg if ACS suspected" (the harness records panels by title only), but nothing turns them into an investigation order or plan action: the only ECG action anywhere is the "12-lead ECG - pre-operative cardiac baseline (age >= 40)" prompt line (or none at 36 years).
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add ECG and hs-troponin as investigation actions of the chest-pain pathway / ACS prompt (today the Chest Pain Pathway checklist is shown as a panel but emits no investigation actions).

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: no troponin investigation. The triage Chest Pain Pathway panel does fire here and its checklist text reads "ECG within 10 minutes", "Troponin (hs-cTnI/T) at 0h and 3h" and "Aspirin 300mg if ACS suspected" (the harness records panels by title only), but nothing turns them into an investigation order or plan action: no troponin in any investigation, plan or prompt output. (The checklist 0 h/3 h sampling also differs from the ESC 2023 0 h/1 h or 0 h/2 h algorithm.)
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add ECG and hs-troponin as investigation actions of the chest-pain pathway / ACS prompt (today the Chest Pain Pathway checklist is shown as a panel but emits no investigation actions).

mustInclude.note: Joint cardiology-obstetric management of ACS in pregnancy.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: none of 4 management items matched (sources: web.clinicalPrompts). First items: • If urine β-HCG positive: serum quantitative β-HCG + urgent TVS — exclude ectopic. | • If ectopic suspected: emergency gynaecology referral — surgical or medical management. | • Confirm cervical smear date — document last result. | • Refer gynaecology — cervical smear overdue (> 3 years)..
mustInclude.proposedFix: Pregnancy-aware prompt: add obstetric review and fetal monitoring whenever pregnancyPossible and an emergency presentation.

mustExclude.note: A plan asserting a negative pregnancy test in a woman at 33 weeks is a wrong-patient-state error.

guideline.name: 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes
guideline.section: Section 3 (triage and diagnosis): 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of first medical contact; hs-cTn 0 h/1 h (or 0 h/2 h) algorithm; atypical presentations (epigastric pain, dyspnoea, fatigue, nausea) more common in women, older people and people with diabetes; aspirin loading dose for all patients without contraindication; STEMI: immediate reperfusion strategy
guideline.citation: Byrne RA, Rossello X, Coughlan JJ, et al. 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes. Eur Heart J. 2023;44:3720-3826.

guideline.name: 2018 ESC Guidelines for the management of cardiovascular diseases during pregnancy
guideline.section: Section 8 (coronary artery disease): ECG and troponin for chest pain in pregnancy; spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is the commonest cause of pregnancy-associated MI; management in a centre with cardiology and obstetric expertise
guideline.citation: Regitz-Zagrosek V, Roos-Hesselink JW, Bauersachs J, et al. Eur Heart J. 2018;39:3165-3241.

rationale: Pregnancy permutation: young, low-risk-looking woman where anchoring on gallstones or anxiety is the failure mode. SCAD is the leading cause of pregnancy-associated MI (ESC 2018).
